changes: OpenClaw shipped fresh betas, with v2026.5.26-beta.1 published on 2026-05-26 21:10 UTC and v2026.5.26-beta.2 on 2026-05-27 05:46 UTC, while the repo stayed highly active through 2026-05-27 07:29 UTC.
PicoClaw posted another nightly build on 2026-05-27 01:09 UTC, preserving the strongest day-to-day release cadence in the cheap-hardware and edge lane.
IronClaw released 0.29.0 on 2026-05-26 16:58 UTC, showing the privacy-and-security lane is still shipping, not just positioning.
HiClaw released v1.1.2 on 2026-05-27 05:59 UTC and SwarmClaw released v1.9.36 on 2026-05-26 14:01 UTC, reinforcing continued motion in the orchestration and control-plane lane.

Hermes Agent, nanobot, ZeroClaw, NanoClaw, Poco, and AstrBot all remained repo-active in the latest snapshot, but there was no taxonomy-changing entrant or strategic repositioning in the monitored set.
whyItMatters: The daily signal is still execution velocity across multiple lanes, not a new category shape: OpenClaw remains the pace-setter, PicoClaw keeps validating the low-cost edge wedge, IronClaw is still advancing the trust-and-security case, and HiClaw plus SwarmClaw keep the multi-agent control-plane lane warm.
The broader ecosystem frame still holds: lighter runtimes, safer runtimes, multi-agent orchestration, and learning-loop or long-running agent behavior remain the durable fault lines.
